_about: Moppetopia, the OnlyWorlds demo world, as keel answered Try a demo world on 2026-11-04 (markers left out; one title renamed Skipper throughout, for the repository word check). Replayed by tests/e2e/strand-picture.spec.ts.

world.name: Moppetopia
world.description: Felt sailors, a water world, and a nebula of stale cookies. Two hundred years after the Treaty of Soft Landings ended the Great Puddle War, the Puddle Navy keeps the peace from the USS Fuzzball, the Eternal Drip keeps everyone damp, and Admiral Fluffington and Skipper Snoot are still not speaking.

character.name: Lieutenant Jonas
character.description: Engineer who works with Skipper Snoot. Trained in The Works (Feltropolis Level 6). Knows every shortcut in the industrial level. Used to work the zero-G looms before becoming a spacer.

character.name: Wrinkles
character.description: Runs Wrinkle's Repairs, an off-the-books ship maintenance operation on Feltropolis Level 3.

character.name: Governor Threadsworth
character.description: Governor of Feltropolis station. Oversees administration from Level 5.

character.name: Old Biscuit
character.description: Elder member of the Cookie Pirates. Remembers the baking days before the Treaty. Tells stories of the old guilds.
character.background: Lived through the disbanding of the Baking Guilds after Treaty of Soft Landings.

character.name: Commander Vex
character.description: Mentioned in Puddle Navy records but personality undeveloped.

character.name: Drizzle
character.description: Bartender at The Soggy Sock tavern on Feltropolis Level 3. A war veteran who lost her color to trauma: she was purple, now she is gray. One of the oldest living moppets at around 260 (born 57 BT). She waters Snoot's drinks because she likes him, and arranged his eye replacement at Feltropolis. Every Year Zero anniversary she sends Admiral Fluffington a drink, and he never touches it. She filed the Soggy Sock Incident Report in Year 203 YSL, when Snoot arrived with a Bakerfolk fragment and a feral moppet on a leash. She has noticed that Madame Threadbare's faded violet felt might be partial decoloration: it takes one to know one.
character.physicality: Gray felt, formerly purple before traumatic decoloration.
character.mentality: She was at Moistened Valley. She doesn't talk about it. She waters Snoot's drinks because she needs him alive more than he does.
character.background: Served in The Great Puddle War. Witnessed the Moistened Valley Massacre. Survived but was traumatically decolored. Now runs a tavern in The Squeeze.

character.name: The Crumbler
character.description: Leader of the Cookie Pirates. Claims to hear The Whispering, ancient Bakerfolk minds preserved in cookie substrate, in the deep Snack Nebula. Wears a helmet of hardened macaron that may be fused to their felt. Makes pilgrimages to the Soft Spot and takes new pirates there as initiation. Possibly an ancient Dry Ones survivor of the Moistened Valley Massacre. Wants the truth told, not revenge. After Skipper Snoot found The Rolling Pin, sent a three-word message: "We're coming home." Nobody knows exactly what it means, but it is the first time the Cookie Pirates have signaled any wish to return to settled space.

character.name: Chief Engineer Wrinkles
character.description: Chief Engineer on the USS Fuzzball. Very old, with faded brown felt, and has served under Admiral Splashworth himself. Knows things about the old days. During the Crumblefield Standoff (Year 197 YSL), Wrinkles stopped Admiral Fluffington from firing on the Stale Vengeance by pointing out that the compressed sugar particles would chain-detonate and destroy both ships. Possibly saved everyone aboard both.
character.background: Served under Admiral Splashworth during The Great Puddle War.

character.name: Thud
character.description: Weapons Officer on the USS Fuzzball. Gray felt. Doesn't talk much. Possibly an ex-Dry One, which would be controversial.
character.mentality: Doesn't talk. Does the job. Nobody's asked too hard about his background and he's not offering.

character.name: Squeaky
character.description: Communications Officer on the USS Fuzzball. Bright green felt. Name is ironic - actually has a very deep voice.

character.name: Doc Stitch
character.description: Medical Officer on the USS Fuzzball. White felt. Specializes in felt repair and googly eye maintenance.

character.name: Rudder
character.description: Helmsman on the USS Fuzzball. Blue felt. Steady, reliable, boring. Foil to Pip's anxiety.

character.name: Sergeant Flop
character.description: Marine Commander on the USS Fuzzball. Orange felt. Leads boarding parties. Has seen too much combat.
character.mentality: Led enough boarding parties that he stopped flinching. Doesn't mean he stopped thinking.
character.background: Extensive combat experience in naval boarding operations.

character.name: Commander Vera
character.description: Possible Claw agent on the USS Fuzzball. Cold and efficient, and rumored to have Claw connections. Either she reports on Fluffington's loyalty to the intelligence organization, or she is loyal to Fluffington and lying to the Claw.
character.mentality: Doesn't waste words or loyalty. Maybe reports on Fluffington to The Claw, maybe doesn't. Either way, she's the most dangerous person on the Fuzzball.

character.name: Nibbles
character.description: Quartermaster of the Cookie Pirates aboard the Stale Vengeance. Counts everything. Every crumb. Literally. Has a ledger made of flattened wafer that tracks cookie debris reserves down to the milligram. The Cookie Pirate Code says never waste crumbs, and Nibbles has made this a personal religion. Tan felt, slightly stale-smelling, with one eye slightly larger than the other (natural, not an injury; it just makes them look permanently suspicious). Joined the pirates after being fired from The Felt Exchange for insisting that traders account for microscopic felt fiber loss during transactions. The Exchange considered this unreasonable. Nibbles considers the Exchange sloppy. Gets along surprisingly well with Pip: they share the obsessive measuring nobody else appreciates.
character.physicality: Tan felt, slight stale smell, asymmetric googly eyes (one slightly larger).
character.mentality: Counts everything. Every crumb. Finds waste the way other moppets find pain: immediate, involuntary, hard to explain to anyone who doesn't feel it.
character.background: Former Felt Exchange auditor, fired for excessive precision. Found purpose in Cookie Pirate logistics.

character.name: Madame Threadbare
character.description: Proprietor of The Thread Market on Feltropolis Level 2. Sells fabric, zero-G woven goods, and information. The information is not on the price list, and costs more than the rest. Her faded violet felt she calls vintage coloring; Drizzle suspects partial decoloration from something Threadbare won't discuss. She has run the Thread Market for 90 years and knows every trade deal, affair and supply-chain irregularity on the station. The Moisture Merchants Guild has tried to recruit her three times. She declined: membership would require financial transparency, which would show how many favors she is owed by how many important moppets. She sends regular fabric samples to The Claw, who she may or may not work for. She also sends fabric samples to Skipper Snoot, who she definitely works for. Playing both sides isn't treachery; it's inventory management.
character.physicality: Faded violet felt (possibly partial decoloration). Elegant, deliberate movements.
character.mentality: Knows things. Sells things. The faction she's actually loyal to is called 'Madame Threadbare.' Has managed 90 years of knowing everyone's business by never being owed by fewer than three parties at once.
character.background: 90 years running The Thread Market. Knows everything about everyone on Feltropolis. Relationship with The Claw and Skipper Snoot simultaneously.

character.name: Professor Fuzz
character.description: Historian at the Museum of Moistened History in Puddleton. Tawny felt, perpetually dusty from archive work, with spectacles balanced on googly eyes that are slightly too large for his face. He has spent 40 years researching The Great Puddle War and has got closer to the truth about the Moistened Valley Massacre than anyone except Skipper Snoot. Unlike Snoot, he doesn't know what he has found. He thinks he is writing a revisionist academic paper about casualty discrepancies. He is assembling a case file. The Claw has noticed. Fuzz has not noticed The Claw. He lives in apartment 4-17-C on Feltropolis Level 4, takes the shuttle down to Puddleton every day, and considers his biggest problem to be the library's inconsistent filing system.
character.physicality: Tawny felt, perpetually dusty. Oversized googly eyes behind spectacles. Shuffling gait from decades of archive corridors.
character.mentality: Obsessively thorough. Academically brilliant, socially oblivious. Cannot tell when he's being followed, watched, or lied to. Thinks the biggest conspiracy in moppet history is a filing error.

character.name: Governor Dampworth
character.description: Station administrator of Feltropolis. Damp blue felt, always slightly moist from nervous perspiration (moppets sweat moisture when stressed, and Dampworth is always stressed). Appointed by the Treaty Council, answerable to the Puddle Navy in practice, and funded by the Moisture Merchants Guild at budget time. He has never been below Level 4 and doesn't know The Squeeze exists, which is how The Squeeze prefers it. He considers his primary achievement the Year 180 YSL Feltropolis Beautification Initiative, which added decorative felt banners to Level 5 corridors. The banners are ugly. Nobody has told him. He believes Feltropolis runs smoothly because of his leadership; it runs smoothly because Madame Threadbare's information network stops most crises before they reach his desk.
character.physicality: Damp blue felt, perpetually moist. Wears a ceremonial sash that's slightly too long. Blinks more than necessary.
character.mentality: Well-meaning but oblivious. Believes in process, procedure, and decorative banners. Has never had an original thought but is excellent at taking credit for other people's.
character.background: Career bureaucrat. Rose through Level 5 administration by outlasting everyone else. The Treaty Council appointed him because he's controllable. The Puddle Navy tolerates him because he signs whatever they put on his desk.

character.name: Skipper Snoot
character.description: Rogue explorer, smuggler, and the one who knows. Faded blue felt, one googly eye missing since the Snack Nebula crash; under the eyepatch there may be the Googly Eye of Truth. He left the Puddle Navy after The Incident (Year 120 YSL) with evidence of the Moistened Valley Massacre cover-up, and has kept it hidden ever since. He drinks at The Soggy Sock, trades with the Cookie Pirates, and buys information from Madame Threadbare at The Thread Market, playing both sides. In Year 203 YSL he found The Rolling Pin past the Crumblefields, a humming Bakerfolk ruin three kilometers long, and brought back a fragment that hums in time with the Eternal Drip's pump cycle.
character.physicality: Faded blue felt. One googly eye missing, behind an eyepatch that may hold the Googly Eye of Truth.
character.mentality: Drinks too much, trusts too little, and is right about almost everything. Left the Navy with the truth and never figured out what to do with it. Still hasn't.
character.background: Naval Academy graduate. Found the massacre evidence and left the Navy under mysterious circumstances (The Incident). Now a rogue explorer and smuggler.
character.reputation: Disgraced ex-officer to the establishment. A folk hero to those who suspect the truth.

character.name: Admiral Fluffington
character.description: Admiral of the Puddle Navy and commander of the USS Fuzzball. Pink felt, immaculately kept, with one googly eye that was Admiral Splashworth's, and with it some of Splashworth's memories. Son of Admiral Stuffington and the last of House Stuffington. He and Skipper Snoot were friends at the Naval Academy until The Incident. His catchphrase: "We sail where the puddles flow." The family crest, three water drops and a felt star, hangs on the Fuzzball's bridge.
character.physicality: Pink felt, immaculately kept. One googly eye, Splashworth's left, transplanted.
character.mentality: Does his job exactly as the Puddle Navy trained him to. Wakes some nights seeing things he didn't live through, and tasting oats, which nobody in Moppetopia eats. It is getting harder to tell where duty ends and denial begins.
character.background: Son of Admiral Stuffington. Naval Academy graduate, then Admiral. Carries Splashworth's eye, and possibly his guilt.

character.name: Admiral Splashworth
character.description: Legendary war hero of The Great Puddle War. He won the Battle of Damp Ridge against impossible odds, and his tactics are still taught at the Naval Academy. He is remembered as dying heroically in battle. His left googly eye was kept and later transplanted into Admiral Fluffington, with fragments of his consciousness.
character.mentality: Saw the battlefield clearer than anyone above him. When it mattered most, he chose right over orders.
character.background: Won the Battle of Damp Ridge. Died in the Moistened Valley, officially in battle.

character.name: Pip
character.description: Navigator on the USS Fuzzball, and its youngest crew member. Pale yellow felt. Nervous, and secretly brilliant. Notices what others miss, and keeps a notebook of numbers nobody asked for. Fluffington dismisses her, though she reminds him of young Snoot. She tracks her own water use obsessively, out of anxiety. When Snoot brought back a fragment from The Rolling Pin, Pip held it up and her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds, a response that should be physically impossible. Her calculations then showed that the fragment's resonance frequency matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle exactly. She looked the way Pip looks when the numbers are very bad and also very interesting.
character.mentality: Notices everything, says half of it, writes down all of it. Has been lying awake for five years about a number nobody else bothered to look at.

character.name: Admiral Stuffington
character.description: Admiral Fluffington's father, officially a war hero who died in the Great Puddle War. A high-ranking Admiral of the Puddle Navy, he wanted the Dry Ones destroyed, not integrated.
character.background: High-ranking Puddle Navy Admiral during The Great Puddle War. Wanted the Dry Ones destroyed, not integrated.
character.motivations: Sought complete destruction of the Dry Ones rather than peaceful integration.

creature.name: Crumb-Eel
creature.description: Long, soft-bodied creature native to the Crumblefields. Burrows through compressed cookie material the way fish move through water. Coravel schools will not enter Crumb-Eel territory. Nibbles maintains they are intelligent on the basis of a single observed eel that returned a dropped wafer to its owner; nobody on the Stale Vengeance argued with him about it. Population unknown. Aggressive only when food is present, which in the Crumblefields is almost always.
creature.appearance: Eight to twelve meters long when fully grown. Hide is felt-textured but waterproof. Senses crumb density gradients across distances up to two kilometers. Reproduces by spawning in dense crumb pockets that compress around the eggs and provide both protection and first meals.
creature.habits: Patrols territorial routes through the deeper Crumblefield strata. Avoids zero-density regions, which it appears to find disorienting. Will follow ships traveling slowly enough to drop crumbs but does not attack hulls.

creature.name: Felt Mite
creature.description: Microscopic parasite found in poorly-maintained felt. Causes color fade in localized patches. Drizzle never had Felt Mites; her decoloration is from something worse. Medical knowledge of Felt Mites is well-developed; they are not feared. They are however considered embarrassing, on the order of a dental cavity.
creature.appearance: Fifteen to thirty micrometers in length. Lives in the felt fiber bed. Feeds on residual moisture and felt-keratin. Visible damage appears after roughly six weeks of infestation as small pale patches that do not return to color even after eradication.
creature.habits: Spread through direct felt-to-felt contact. Treatment is straightforward and over-the-counter; the social cost of admitting one needs the treatment is the actual problem.

creature.name: Oven-Wisp
creature.description: Heat phenomenon found near The Soft Spot. Possibly residual Bakerfolk consciousness, possibly just a warm spot that moves. Cookie Pirates leave biscuits for them; the biscuits disappear. Whether they are eaten or whether they are simply moved by the same drift that moves the wisps is an open question that nobody has tried very hard to answer because the current arrangement is working.
creature.appearance: Not biological in any standard sense. Localized temperature elevation, two to four degrees above ambient, moving at unpredictable but not random speeds. Lifespan unknown; the same wisp may persist for years or may not be the same wisp at all.
creature.habits: Concentrates around the Soft Spot's inner ring during the long summers and disperses into the outer Snack Nebula during winter. Whether wisps respond to attention is debated; Old Biscuit believes they do, and Old Biscuit has more time with them than anyone.

creature.name: Sock-Stalker
creature.description: Feral creature inhabiting Feltropolis' unused service corridors. Said to live on dropped felt fibers and discarded googly-eye liquid. Maintenance workers on Level 6 swear it sings at shift change. The administration has classified it as a rumor for forty years and has quietly increased the maintenance budget for service corridor lighting by twelve percent during the same period.
creature.appearance: Approximately one meter at the shoulder. Quadrupedal. Felt is matted and stained but not damaged in the way one would expect after decades of corridor life, which has led some researchers to argue that Sock-Stalkers regenerate felt internally, which would be unprecedented for any moppet-adjacent species.
creature.habits: Nocturnal. Avoids contact. Has never been recorded attacking a moppet, though it has been recorded approaching one within four meters during shift change and then retreating. The singing is not confirmed but is described consistently across forty years of accounts as 'low and tired.'

creature.name: Vacuum Coravel
creature.description: Larger cousin of the standard Coravel. Found only in deep Snack Nebula. Considered very good luck because nobody who has seen one has ever needed luck again. This is reported by spacers as a positive omen; researchers note it is also consistent with terminal navigation events.
creature.appearance: Up to six meters in length, compared to the standard Coravel's forty centimeters. Bioluminescent across the flank. Survives vacuum through a method that has been studied for one hundred and seventy years without conclusive findings. Believed to be solitary; no Vacuum Coravel has ever been recorded in proximity to another.
creature.habits: Drifts. Does not appear to feed. Does not appear to seek shelter. Will pass within meters of a ship without registering on standard sensors. Recordings exist; spacers who have seen them in person say the recordings do not capture it.

creature.name: Contraband
creature.description: A Coravel, one of the school that follows the Leaky Bucket on every run, and the one the whole crew knows by name. Snoot says he will not feed it. He feeds it whatever he can't sell, and hardtack when there is nothing else.

creature.name: The Mother
creature.description: Something lives in the reservoir under the Eternal Drip. The pumps run down to it, and the water that rises back through the filters smells warm and a little sour.
creature.appearance: Nobody has seen it. The reservoir is a pale lake that bubbles slowly.
creature.habits: The pumps feed it. What rises back is what the moppets drink.

family.name: House Stuffington
family.description: The preeminent naval dynasty of Puddleton. Three generations of Admirals, or two, depending on what you believe. Admiral Stuffington (the patriarch) is officially deceased, a war hero who gave everything for the Puddle Navy. Admiral Fluffington (his son) carries the name with pink-felted dignity and an inherited compass. The family crest features three water drops and a felt star, which adorns the USS Fuzzball's bridge. There are no other known Stuffingtons, which makes Fluffington the last of the line, a fact he drinks about more than he'd admit.
family.spirit: Naval service is expected, not chosen. Every Stuffington takes the salt (absorption of seawater) before their tenth birthday. The family compass passes to the eldest serving officer.

species.name: Puddle Moppet
species.description: The standard moppet subtype. Water-absorbing, traditional, mostly found in Puddleton.
species.appearance: Vibrant felt colors (pink, blue, orange, green, purple). Standard googly eyes that are functional organs, not decorations.
species.instincts: Absorb moisture through felt. Drawn to water sources.
species.communication: Googly eye pupil movements convey meaning and emotion.

species.name: Dust Moppet
species.description: Also called The Dry Ones. Not evil, just different absorption needs - they were starving during the war. Mostly integrated into moppet society after The Great Puddle War, though some holdouts exist in the Snack Nebula as Cookie Pirates. Their knowledge of surviving without water was suppressed after the Treaty.
species.appearance: Rougher felt texture like burlap. Browns, tans, grays (natural coloring, not trauma-induced).
species.instincts: Absorb minerals, dust, and dry particulates instead of moisture.
species.communication: Googly eye movements, similar to Puddle Moppets.

species.name: Space Moppet
species.description: Evolved or adapted over 200 years in Feltropolis orbital station. Cultural or biological distinction unclear.
species.appearance: Thinner, more vacuum-resistant felt. Paler, pastel colors. Slightly larger googly eyes, possibly adapted to station lighting.
species.instincts: Can survive brief vacuum exposure (10-15 minutes).

species.name: Feral Moppet
species.description: Live in wild areas between settlements. Lost their googly eyes somehow and navigate by touch. Felt is matted and dirty. Terrifying to civilized moppets. Used by Cookie Pirates as scouts because they feel vibrations in crumbs. Two populations: born-feral and became-feral (who remember civilization and are sadder).
species.appearance: Matted, dirty felt. No googly eyes.
species.instincts: Navigate by touch instead of sight. Feel vibrations in surrounding materials.
species.sociality: Live in wild areas, away from civilization.

species.name: Coravel
species.description: Space fish. Swim through vacuum somehow. Found near Feltropolis in schools. Considered good luck by spacers. One school follows Skipper Snoot's ship, the Leaky Bucket.
species.appearance: Fish-like creatures that exist in vacuum.

species.name: Moppet
species.description: The people of Moppetopia: small felt creatures with googly eyes, who eat by absorbing moisture. Puddle Moppets, Dust Moppets, Space Moppets and Feral Moppets are its kinds.

species.name: The Whispering
species.description: Ancient Bakerfolk minds preserved in cookie substrate in the deep Snack Nebula. Not evil, just lonely. Hungry to be remembered. The Crumbler hears them. Speaks without speaking: non-physical, incorporeal communication.
species.appearance: Unknown. Non-physical presence in cookie debris.
species.communication: Speaks without speaking. Preserved consciousness communicating across time.

species.name: Bakerfolk
species.description: Ancient pre-moppet civilization. Created the Snack Nebula ovens. Vanished: possibly evolved into moppets, ascended, or went extinct. No living examples. Evidence includes ancient artifacts, the Googly Eye of Truth, and architectural ruins in deep Puddleton caves. Their minds may be preserved in cookie substrate in the Snack Nebula (The Whispering).

institution.name: Baking Guilds
institution.description: Ancient institutions of the Dry Ones that practiced baking arts. Disbanded after the Treaty of Soft Landings under Article 7, which banned weaponized crumbs. Their descendants became the Cookie Pirates.
institution.doctrine: Baking traditions passed down from possibly the ancient Bakerfolk.
institution.status: Disbanded after Treaty of Soft Landings. Descendants fled to Snack Nebula.

institution.name: Moisture Merchants Guild
institution.description: The trade association governing absorption station vendors on Feltropolis Level 2. Runs fourteen licensed stations dispensing flavored moisture - salted puddle (classic), nebula mist (tangy), deep drip (premium, supposedly from the Eternal Drip source itself, actually just regular water with marketing). Membership requires a felting license and a clean absorption record. The Guild's real power is controlling moisture quality standards, which means controlling who gets to sell drinks on the station. Drizzle's Soggy Sock on Level 3 operates without Guild membership, which the Guild pretends not to notice because nobody wants to argue with a 260-year-old war veteran who saw things.
institution.doctrine: Quality moisture for quality moppets. Fourteen approved flavors. No unauthorized absorption stations above Level 3.

institution.name: Puddle Navy
institution.description: The fleet of Puddleton, which fights in puddles and in space. Its Academy still teaches Splashworth's tactics from Damp Ridge.

institution.name: The Claw
institution.description: Secret police and intelligence organization. Symbol is claw marks (scratch pattern). Agents hidden throughout the Puddle Navy and civilian life. Relationship to Admiral Fluffington unclear: either it reports to him or it operates above him. Monitors loyalty.
institution.doctrine: Watch everyone. Report everything. Erase what doesn't fit.
institution.status: Active and secretive. Extent of influence unknown.

institution.name: Treaty Council
institution.description: Governing body with authority over Treaty-related matters. Controls The Locked Room on Feltropolis Level 7. Neither Puddleton nor the Feltropolis governor has access to its jurisdiction.
institution.doctrine: Maintain neutrality and enforce the provisions of the Treaty of Soft Landings.
institution.status: Active. Controls classified Treaty assets and prisoners.

collective.name: The Drippers
collective.description: A small cabal of Felt Exchange traders who've noticed something nobody else has: micro-fluctuations in water delivery volume from the Eternal Drip pipeline. They don't know about the ancient machine underneath. They don't know about Pip's measurements. They just see the numbers wobbling, and they're buying long-term drought options at 3 felt-marks each while everyone else laughs at them. 'Drought insurance? The Drip is ETERNAL, you soggy fool.' The Drippers smile and buy more. Their leader, a trader known only as Damp Margot, keeps a private ledger of delivery volumes going back 30 years. The fluctuations started 8 years ago. She doesn't know what's causing them. She just knows which way to bet. If Pip ever walked into The Felt Exchange and looked at Margot's ledger, the two datasets together would confirm the crisis beyond any doubt. They have never met.
collective.composition: Five to eight Felt Exchange traders, led by Damp Margot. Mix of veteran commodity traders and younger analysts who followed Margot's numbers.
collective.activity: Quietly accumulating drought options and water futures positions. Diversifying felt-mark holdings into physical goods. Building reserve moisture stockpiles in private storage on Level 4.

collective.name: The Quiet Register
collective.description: The short list of those who know Admiral Stuffington is alive, besides Stuffington himself. The Treaty Council keeps it, and has never let it get long.

collective.name: The Valley Silence
collective.description: Those who know what happened in the Moistened Valley, and do not say. Drizzle is one.

collective.name: Cookie Pirates
collective.description: Not criminals: refugees. Descendants of the old Dry Ones bakers who fled to the Snack Nebula after the Treaty of Soft Landings disbanded the Baking Guilds (Treaty Article 7 banned weaponized crumbs). Led by The Crumbler. Live by the Cookie Pirate Code. Make pilgrimages to the Soft Spot. Signature combat maneuver: The Stale Roll, a full-speed lateral spin that turns the Stale Vengeance into a spinning battering ram. Nibbles serves as quartermaster, tracking every crumb in a wafer ledger.
collective.composition: Descendants of Dust Moppet (Dry Ones) bakers and massacre survivors who fled after the Treaty.
collective.activity: Operate in the Snack Nebula. Trade occasionally with outsiders like Skipper Snoot. Preserve Bakerfolk heritage.

location.name: Snack Nebula
location.description: Dangerous asteroid field made of stale cookies that clogs ship engines.

location.name: The Drying Chamber
location.description: Forbidden zero-humidity territory and former stronghold of the Dry Ones.

location.name: Museum of Moistened History
location.description: Museum in Puddleton, where Professor Fuzz is the historian. It keeps the earliest copy of the Moistened Valley Account, behind glass so thick that the text cannot be read.
location.function: Preserves and displays historical artifacts and accounts.

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 1: The Docks
location.description: Where ships come in. Massive felt airlocks seal against vacuum. Puddle Navy has reserved berths Alpha through Echo. Civilian berths on outer ring. The Quarantine Zone handles ships from Snack Nebula with cookie contamination protocols.

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 2: Commerce
location.description: Markets, shops, trade halls. Where Feltropolis makes its money. Includes The Felt Exchange, Googly Eye Emporium, The Thread Market, and absorption stations (flavored moisture dispensers).

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 4: Residential
location.description: Where people live. Standard felt-pod apartments (small, cozy, humid) and The Luxury Tier (rich merchants, drier climate, controversial). Professor Fuzz has apartment 4-17-C here.
location.function: Living quarters for station workers and permanent residents.

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 5: Administration
location.description: Government offices. Trade regulations, customs, diplomacy. Contains Governor's Office, Treaty Hall (where Treaty of Soft Landings anniversary is celebrated), and Puddle Navy Liaison Office (Fluffington hates coming here).

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 6: The Works
location.description: Industrial level where felt production happens. Zero-G Looms (famous space-grade felt), The Vats (raw materials to felt fiber, smells weird), and Engineering (station maintenance, power systems). Jonas trained here.
location.form: Industrial factory floor with zero-gravity manufacturing.

location.name: The Felt Exchange
location.description: Raw material trading market on Feltropolis Level 2. Also home to Puddle Futures trading - speculative financial instruments on water allocations from the Eternal Drip. A group of traders called 'the Drippers' have noticed micro-fluctuations and are buying drought options. Former employee Nibbles was fired for insisting traders account for microscopic felt fiber loss.

location.name: Googly Eye Emporium
location.description: Replacement eyes, custom calibrations, and repairs on Feltropolis Level 2.

location.name: The Thread Market
location.description: Fabric supplies and zero-G woven goods on Feltropolis Level 2.

location.name: The Dry Room
location.description: Gambling den on Feltropolis Level 3. Ironic name given moppet culture.

location.name: Wrinkle's Repairs
location.description: Off-the-books ship maintenance run by Wrinkles on Feltropolis Level 3.
location.function: Gray market ship repairs and modifications.

location.name: The Quarantine Zone
location.description: Part of Feltropolis Level 1 docks. Ships coming from Snack Nebula undergo cookie contamination protocols here.
location.form: Isolated docking berths with decontamination systems.

location.name: The Lookout
location.description: Public observation deck on Feltropolis Level 7 with gorgeous views of the Snack Nebula.

location.name: Feltropolis Defense Center
location.description: Defense systems on Feltropolis Level 7. Supposedly just sensors but probably weapons.

location.name: Treaty Hall
location.description: Venue on Feltropolis Level 5 where the Treaty of Soft Landings anniversary is celebrated.

location.name: The Soft Spot
location.description: Area within the Snack Nebula where cookies somehow stayed chewy instead of going stale. Possibly the heart of Bakerfolk civilization still warm, or active ovens still functioning. Sacred to the Cookie Pirates. The Crumbler makes pilgrimages here and takes new pirates as initiation.
location.form: Region of anomalously fresh cookie debris with residual warmth.
location.function: Spiritual site for Cookie Pirates. Navigation landmark. Pilgrimage destination.

location.name: The Soggy Sock
location.description: Tavern on Feltropolis Level 3. Bartender is Drizzle. Snoot drinks here in his corner booth when on station.

location.name: The Leaky Bucket
location.description: Skipper Snoot's ship. Name is ironic because puddle ships need to be watertight. Usually docks at Berth 7-G at Feltropolis when in port - unofficial reserved spot because the dock master owes Snoot a favor.
location.form: Felt-based spacecraft. Capable of water and space travel.
location.function: Personal vessel for Skipper Snoot and his crew.

location.name: Whisper Gallery
location.description: Information broker establishment on Feltropolis Level 3. Proprietor unnamed and mysterious.

location.name: Drip Plaza
location.description: Central gathering point in Puddleton, with a statue of Admiral Splashworth. Rumor says the statue is hollow, with something hidden inside.

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 3: The Squeeze
location.description: Where all the unofficial business happens. Named for its narrow corridors where moppets squeeze past each other: good for privacy, bad for fire evacuation. Home to The Soggy Sock tavern, Wrinkle's Repairs, The Dry Room gambling den, and Whisper Gallery information broker.

location.name: Feltropolis - Level 7: The Spire
location.description: Top of the spindle. Contains The Lookout (public observation with gorgeous Snack Nebula views), Feltropolis Defense Center (supposedly sensors but probably weapons), and The Locked Room (controlled by the Treaty Council).

location.name: Crumblefields
location.description: Areas of pure cookie debris within the Snack Nebula. A navigation nightmare, with zero visibility and constant crumb clouds. Site of the Crumblefield Standoff (Year 197 YSL): the USS Fuzzball and the Stale Vengeance faced off but neither fired, since a weapons discharge would ignite the compressed sugar particles. Now effectively Cookie Pirate territory by mutual unspoken agreement.
location.form: Dense fields of cookie fragments and dust.
location.function: Navigation hazard. Requires feral moppet scouts to traverse safely.

location.name: The Rolling Pin
location.description: Ancient Bakerfolk ruin found by Skipper Snoot beyond the Crumblefields in Year 203 YSL. About three kilometers long, and shaped like its namesake. It is humming: ancient technology that should be inert is still running. Not the Soft Spot; a previously unknown site.
location.form: Massive cylindrical structure resembling a rolling pin, approximately three kilometers in length. Humming with unexplained energy.
location.function: Unknown. Ancient Bakerfolk construction, purpose not yet determined.

location.name: Feltropolis
location.description: Orbital space station and primary manufacturing hub for felt technology: a spindle of seven levels, from The Docks at the bottom to The Spire at the top.

location.name: Naval Academy
location.description: Training facility in Puddleton where Admiral Fluffington and Skipper Snoot studied together. Teaches Admiral Splashworth's tactics. Near a major library used by Professor Fuzz.
location.function: Trains officers for the Puddle Navy.

location.name: Soggia
location.description: The moppets' home planet: puddled, felt-soft, and mostly damp, under Feltropolis's orbit. Puddleton sits on it, and the Eternal Drip rises from its reservoir. The island map is Soggia's own.
location.function: Home planet; the water and the puddles come from here

location.name: Puddleton
location.description: Capital city of moppet civilization. A water-based metropolis built around the Eternal Drip.

location.name: The Locked Room
location.description: Classified space on Feltropolis Level 7, controlled by the Treaty Council. Neither Puddleton nor the station governor has access. Rumor says it also holds the Googly Eye of Truth, though others say Snoot's eyepatch does.
location.form: Secured chamber with life support for immortal prisoner.
location.function: Classified storage under Treaty Council jurisdiction.

location.name: The Eternal Drip
location.description: The sacred water source at the heart of Puddleton and the lifeblood of moppet civilization. Its pumping station feeds the pipeline to Feltropolis and the fourteen licensed absorption stations.
location.form: Ancient pumping and filtration machine disguised as natural spring. Constant flow of processed water.
location.function: Sacred water source. Lifeblood of moppet civilization.

object.name: USS Fuzzball
object.description: Flagship of the Puddle Navy commanded by Admiral Fluffington.

object.name: Felt Cruiser
object.description: Standard military vessel class used by the Puddle Navy.

object.name: The Squeezed Sponge
object.description: Merchant vessel operating in moppet space.

object.name: Drip Drop
object.description: Courier ship known for fast delivery.

object.name: Medal of Damp Valor
object.description: Puddle Navy military decoration featuring a three-splash insignia. Worn by Admiral Fluffington.

object.name: Stale Vengeance
object.description: The Cookie Pirates' ship, built from compressed cookie material and somehow space-worthy. Feltropolis engineers can't figure out how it works. Possibly uses ancient Bakerfolk technology. It can execute The Stale Roll.
object.aesthetics: Constructed from compressed cookies - brown, textured, stale.

object.name: Googly Eye of Truth
object.description: Ancient precursor artifact: a First Fuzzy One's preserved consciousness in googly eye form. Possibly hidden in The Locked Room on Feltropolis Level 7, or possibly in the socket under Snoot's eyepatch (he found it in the Snack Nebula crash, traded it to the Cookie Pirates for safe passage, and they gave it back because The Crumbler couldn't bear its visions). If Snoot has it, this is why he sees things and drinks. Precursor to modern Googly Eye Technology.
object.utility: Unknown. Shows visions of truth. Possibly contains advanced consciousness or navigation capabilities.
object.origins: Created by the ancient Bakerfolk/First Fuzzy Ones civilization. Contains preserved consciousness.

object.name: USS Splashworth
object.description: Puddle Navy ship named posthumously after Admiral Splashworth as an honor. Naval tradition is not to name ships after living admirals.

object.name: Splashworth's Compass
object.description: Old compass that belonged to Admiral Splashworth, now carried by Admiral Fluffington as a keepsake. Nobody knows whether it works. Some say it points to the truth.
object.utility: Navigation device. Possibly symbolic or magical guidance.
object.origins: Belonged to Admiral Splashworth during The Great Puddle War.

object.name: Deep Drip
object.description: The Moisture Merchants Guild's premium product line. Marketed as 'pure Eternal Drip source water, naturally filtered through ancient geological formations' with a label featuring a stylized water drop and the words 'From the Heart of the World.' It's regular station water run through an extra pipe that adds trace minerals for taste. Costs 12 felt-marks per absorption, four times the price of standard salted puddle. The moppets who buy it insist they can taste the difference. They can't. The extra pipe doesn't even connect to the Eternal Drip. The Guild knows this. The label designer knows this. Governor Dampworth drinks it exclusively and has given the Guild a commendation for 'excellence in hydration.' It is, after the Treaty of Soft Landings itself, possibly the most successful lie in moppet civilization.
object.aesthetics: Elegant glass vessels with gold-leaf labeling. The stylized water drop logo. Premium felt-wrapped dispensers on Level 2.
object.utility: Overpriced water. Status symbol. Proof that marketing works on moppets too.
object.origins: Created by the Moisture Merchants Guild approximately 50 years ago. Has survived three attempted fraud investigations, each of which concluded that 'premium hydration perception is subjective.'

object.name: The Fragment
object.description: A piece of The Rolling Pin retrieved by Skipper Snoot during his latest unauthorized expedition past the Crumblefields. Approximately fist-sized, warm to the touch, smells distinctly of cinnamon. Composition unknown: not felt, not cookie, not any material Feltropolis engineers recognize. When Pip held the Fragment near her instruments, her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds, an involuntary response that shouldn't be physically possible. Her calculations revealed the Fragment's resonance frequency matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle exactly. This is either the most important archaeological discovery in moppet history or the thing that destroys moppet civilization. Possibly both. Currently hidden somewhere on the USS Fuzzball, known only to Snoot, Pip, and Drizzle.
object.aesthetics: Warm, cinnamon-scented fragment of ancient Bakerfolk construction material.
object.utility: Proof that Bakerfolk technology underlies moppet infrastructure. Also: makes Pip's eyes do something impossible.
object.origins: Bakerfolk construction. Retrieved from The Rolling Pin, Year 203 YSL.

construct.name: Googly Eye Technology
construct.description: Moppets use their eyes for more than seeing: navigation, scanning, lie detection. Most of the Navy's operational technology runs through them.

construct.name: Weaponized Crumbs
construct.description: Banned technology or technique mentioned in Treaty of Soft Landings Article 7. Led to the disbanding of the Baking Guilds.
construct.rationale: Crumb-based warfare technique developed by the Baking Guilds during the famine war.
construct.history: Used during The Great Puddle War. Deemed too dangerous post-war.

construct.name: Zero-Gravity Puddle Combat
construct.description: Naval warfare technique adapted for space operations. The Puddle Navy operates in both water and zero-gravity environments.
construct.rationale: The puddle works in space. Nobody knows why. The Navy stopped asking.
construct.history: Developed after the Treaty of Soft Landings when the Puddle Navy expanded to space operations.

construct.name: Zero-Gravity Felt Weaving
construct.description: Technique for producing higher quality felt in zero-gravity conditions. Primary method used at Feltropolis.
construct.rationale: No gravity means no sag. Turns out moppet felt is better when nothing's pulling at it.
construct.history: Enabled the felt technology revolution after the Treaty of Soft Landings.

construct.name: Space-Grade Felt
construct.description: High-quality felt produced through zero-gravity weaving. Waterproof AND space-worthy. Triple-layered construction. Used for ship hulls and station construction.
construct.rationale: Stronger than regular felt. Waterproof and vacuum-rated, which is a weird thing to need but here we are.

construct.name: Felt Technology Revolution
construct.description: Two hundred years of not fighting meant two hundred years of figuring out what felt could do. Feltropolis became the center of it.
construct.history: Began after the Treaty of Soft Landings. Led to space-grade felt, googly eye advances, and expanded naval operations.

construct.name: Puddle Navy Rank System
construct.description: Hierarchical military rank structure of the Puddle Navy. Includes Admiral, Commander, Lieutenant Commander, First Officer, Chief Engineer, Navigator, Weapons Officer, Communications Officer, Medical Officer, Helmsman, Marine Commander, Sergeant.
construct.rationale: Someone has to know who to blame. The rank system handles that.

construct.name: Compressed Cookie Material
construct.description: Structural material used by the Cookie Pirates to build the Stale Vengeance. Somehow space-worthy despite being made from cookies. Feltropolis engineers cannot determine how it works.
construct.rationale: Unknown. Possibly related to ancient Bakerfolk technology or baking guild secrets.
construct.reach: Known only to the Cookie Pirates.

construct.name: Felt Repair
construct.description: Medical technique for repairing damaged moppet felt. Practiced by medical officers like Doc Stitch. Essential for treating injuries.
construct.rationale: Felt regenerates during sleep but can be damaged faster than it heals. Repair techniques accelerate recovery.

construct.name: Soft Spot Pilgrimage
construct.description: Sacred Cookie Pirates ritual. The Crumbler worships the Soft Spot and makes pilgrimages there. New pirates are taken to the Soft Spot as part of initiation. The area's anomalous warmth and preservation have spiritual significance - heart of Bakerfolk civilization.
construct.rationale: The warmth is real and old and shouldn't be there. The Crumbler treats that as proof enough.

construct.name: Moppet Sleep Cycle
construct.description: Moppets require sleep to process absorbed nutrients and regenerate felt. Sleep is when felt heals from damage and restores color. Moppets can have nightmares. Night watch on ships remains necessary despite excellent googly eye night vision.
construct.rationale: Skip sleep and your felt goes ratty. That's the whole rule.

construct.name: Puddle Futures
construct.description: Speculative financial instruments traded at The Felt Exchange on Feltropolis Level 2. Traders buy and sell rights to future water allocations from the Eternal Drip pipeline. Prices have been stable for decades because everyone assumes the Drip is, well, eternal. A small group of traders called 'the Drippers' have noticed micro-fluctuations in delivery volume and are quietly buying long-term drought options. They think they're being clever. Pip could tell them they're being optimistic. Current price of a standard puddle future: 340 felt-marks. Price of a drought option: 3 felt-marks. That ratio is about to become very interesting.
construct.rationale: A financial market built on the assumption that water supply is infinite and the Eternal Drip is a natural phenomenon. Both assumptions are wrong. If either becomes public knowledge, the derivatives structure does not bend: it stops.

construct.name: Generational Trauma
construct.description: The accumulated damage from The Great Puddle War and the Moistened Valley Massacre, still running through moppet society two hundred years later. It shows up as color loss in felt (Drizzle), institutions that operate by not asking certain questions, and a cultural cheerfulness that is slightly too loud. 'We sail where the puddles flow' is what you say to convince yourself the world is not built on blood. The silliness is not denial exactly, but it's doing the same job. Moppets who push past it, like Snoot, get ostracized. Moppets who saw it directly, like Drizzle, go quiet. The googly-eyed aesthetic started somewhere, and nobody talks about where.
construct.rationale: A name, not a force. Moppet society needed a word for what the Great Puddle War and the Moistened Valley Massacre left behind: the decoloration, the silence, the institutions that function by not asking certain questions. Generational Trauma is what you call it when the damage is too distributed to blame on anyone specific.

construct.name: The Treaty Reckoning
construct.description: How Moppetopia counts its years: back from the Treaty of Soft Landings (BT, before the Treaty) and forward from it (YSL, years since Soft Landings). Year 0 is the Treaty, which the Treaty Council celebrates every year in Drip Plaza.

construct.name: Institutional Cover-Up
construct.description: The system of lies, suppression, and narrative control that conceals the truth about the Moistened Valley Massacre. Maintained by the Puddle Navy leadership, the Treaty Council, and The Claw. Splashworth is remembered as a war hero who died in battle, not murdered by his own side. Admiral Stuffington's war crime is erased from history (he's secretly imprisoned, not dead). The Treaty is celebrated as peaceful resolution, not a cover-up. Professor Fuzz's research is getting close to the truth but he doesn't realize he's uncovering a conspiracy.
construct.rationale: The Navy cannot admit what happened at Moistened Valley without admitting it killed Splashworth to keep it quiet. The Fluffington family cannot survive that admission. So: social stability.
construct.history: Began at Year 0 with the Treaty signing and Stuffington's imprisonment. Maintained through control of historical records, pressure on witnesses like Drizzle, and removal of truth-seekers like Snoot.
construct.status: Active for two hundred years. Cracks forming: Snoot has proof, Pip has data, Fuzz has research, and Drizzle is old enough that the cover-up may outlive her usefulness as a silenced witness. The Navy is running out of time to keep the story straight.

construct.name: Cookie Pirate Code
construct.description: Code of conduct followed by the Cookie Pirates. Rules: 1) Never waste crumbs. 2) What's stale is sacred. 3) The third rule is not written down, and nobody will say what it is.
construct.rationale: Rules are rules, even on a pirate ship. Especially when the ship is made of cookies.

construct.name: Year Zero Anniversary
construct.description: Annual commemoration of the Treaty of Soft Landings signing (Year 0). Celebrated throughout moppet space. Drizzle has a private tradition: every anniversary she sends Admiral Fluffington a drink. He never touches it. Neither of them explains it.
construct.rationale: Commemorates peace and the founding of the current calendar system. Also commemorates a war crime.
construct.history: Celebrated for 200 years since the Treaty.

construct.name: Traumatic Decoloration
construct.description: Phenomenon where moppets can lose their original felt color through severe trauma. Example: Drizzle was purple, now gray, after the war.
construct.rationale: Bad enough to bleach your felt. Not a metaphor: the color actually goes.
construct.history: Documented effect from The Great Puddle War. Permanent condition.

construct.name: We Sail Where the Puddles Flow
construct.description: The Puddle Navy's motto, and Admiral Fluffington's catchphrase. Moppets say it at launches and at funerals, in the same voice.
construct.rationale: Admiral Fluffington's catchphrase and the Puddle Navy's unofficial motto. On the surface: heroic naval tradition, brave explorers following water wherever it leads. Underneath: a coping mechanism so effective it became cultural infrastructure. You say it when you need to keep moving and cannot afford to look down. The puddles flow, you follow them, and you do not ask where they came from or what they are flowing over. Every moppet who repeats it is participating in a collective act of looking forward instead of back. The silliness is load-bearing.
construct.history: Origin unclear and deliberately unexamined. Some credit Splashworth himself, which would make it devastating irony given how he actually died. Others say it predates the Navy entirely -- an old Puddleton saying from before moppets left the surface. The Treaty Council has never officially endorsed it, which is the surest sign they find it useful. By Year 200 it had migrated from naval slang to civilian greeting, school motto, and Feltropolis tourism tagline. Madame Threadbare sells embroidered versions at The Thread Market. They are her third-highest margin item.
construct.status: Culturally ubiquitous. Repeated by sailors and civilians, printed on merchandise, taught to children. Comforts and deflects in equal measure. Enables the continued functioning of a society built on suppressed truth. The Crumbler reportedly heard it for the first time via intercepted Navy comms and laughed for three minutes straight.

construct.name: Absorption Rituals
construct.description: Moppet ceremonies built around moisture absorption. Coming of age: first time absorbing directly from the Eternal Drip. Marriage: absorbing from the same source at the same time. Funeral: releasing all moisture back to the cycle. Naval: 'taking the salt,' absorbing seawater before first deployment. The rituals are sincere. They also keep everyone attached to a system nobody questions.
construct.rationale: Ties every major life moment to the water system, which makes the system feel sacred rather than mechanical. Convenient for whoever controls the Eternal Drip.
construct.history: Ancient practices, possibly predating the Treaty.
construct.status: Still happening. Nobody's questioned them. That may be the point.

construct.name: The Stale Roll
construct.description: The Cookie Pirates' signature combat maneuver: a full-speed lateral spin using the Stale Vengeance's unusual hull geometry. Because the ship is built from compressed cookie material, which is harder than any felt-based armor when properly aged, the Stale Roll turns the entire vessel into a spinning battering ram. Feltropolis naval analysts have studied recovered sensor data and concluded the maneuver shouldn't work. The cookie hull should shatter on impact. It doesn't. They have written four papers about why it doesn't. The Cookie Pirates have not read any of them. The Crumbler claims the technique was taught to them by The Whispering, which the analysts find even more irritating than the physics violation.
construct.rationale: Exploits the inexplicable structural properties of compressed cookie material. Effectiveness increases with staleness of hull. The Puddle Navy has no counter-maneuver because they can't replicate the hull material to test against.

construct.name: First Fuzzy Ones' Machine
construct.description: The Eternal Drip is not a natural spring. It is a machine, built by the pre-moppet civilization (the Bakerfolk, the First Fuzzy Ones of moppet legend), with filtration systems, an underground reservoir and pumps. The whole moppet civilization runs on someone else's infrastructure. The machine was built, which means it can break, and it is failing with no one maintaining it.
construct.rationale: Someone built a machine, then vanished, and moppets spent a thousand years calling it sacred water. The machine still runs. Barely.
construct.history: Built by the First Fuzzy Ones before they vanished. Has run for over 1000 years with minimal maintenance needs. Now degrading.
construct.status: Failing. Currently deteriorating at 0.3% per year (accelerating).

construct.name: Every kind
construct.description: The whole world, one row of each kind it holds: the schema shown by example. No anchors; nothing is kept back.

construct.name: The moppets
construct.description: The world read through its people: the five moppet species and the one house, and everything that stands one step from them.

construct.name: Who's who
construct.description: Every moppet, beast and officer of Moppetopia in one list: the people of the world, nothing else. For a visitor who wants to know who lives here.
construct.rationale: Every moppet, beast and officer of Moppetopia in one list: the people of the world, nothing else. For a visitor who wants to know who lives here.

construct.name: The places
construct.description: Where Moppetopia happens: its towns, waters, nebulae and the zones they fall in. For a visitor who wants the map before the story.
construct.rationale: Where Moppetopia happens: its towns, waters, nebulae and the zones they fall in. For a visitor who wants the map before the story.

construct.name: The war years
construct.description: The Great Puddle War and what came of it, year 230 to the founding of Feltropolis: six events in order. For a visitor who wants the history in one sitting.
construct.rationale: The Great Puddle War and what came of it, year 230 to the founding of Feltropolis: six events in order. For a visitor who wants the history in one sitting.

construct.name: The Eternal Drip
construct.description: The long trouble that followed the peace, year 370 to the present: the Drip's events and nothing older. For a visitor who wants to know what is wrong now.
construct.rationale: The long trouble that followed the peace, year 370 to the present: the Drip's events and nothing older. For a visitor who wants to know what is wrong now.

construct.name: Admiral Fluffington's web
construct.description: Everything one step from the Admiral: the people, places, things, stories and events his life touches. For a visitor who wants one character and the world around them.
construct.rationale: Everything one step from the Admiral: the people, places, things, stories and events his life touches. For a visitor who wants one character and the world around them.

construct.name: The spine
construct.description: Moppetopia in six: the navy, its admiral, two cities, the war and the treaty that ended it, each with a line on why it matters. For a visitor with two minutes.
construct.rationale: Moppetopia in six: the navy, its admiral, two cities, the war and the treaty that ended it, each with a line on why it matters. For a visitor with two minutes.

notes.0695db83-8ce7-7510-8000-5f44d31b8f79: The old town the war was fought over.
notes.0695db83-972a-74da-8000-262f1559a7f1: The city founded when the war ended; the world's capital of soft things.
notes.0695db83-afd7-76ee-8000-00f4295f8866: The admiral at the centre of the war, the peace and the rivalry that outlived both.
notes.0695db83-c6e8-7ab6-8000-bf4b7d713f37: The most-linked thing in the world: the navy nearly everyone serves, fights or fears.
notes.0695db83-e681-7a14-8000-5f411a586fb6: The war that shaped everything after it.
notes.0695db83-f0d2-71c5-8000-f74fac372c98: The peace, and the world's year zero.

construct.name: Moistened Valley, three tellings
construct.description: One event and the stories told about it: the massacre, who was there, and the three accounts that do not agree. For a visitor who likes a world that argues with itself.
construct.rationale: One event and the stories told about it: the massacre, who was there, and the three accounts that do not agree. For a visitor who likes a world that argues with itself.

ability.name: Splashworth's Glimpse
ability.description: Involuntary flashes of memory from Splashworth's transplanted left eye. Triggered unpredictably, such as by the smell of salt water, certain angles of light through a viewport, or the sound of orders given in a voice that sounds too much like his father's. For a fraction of a second, Fluffington sees what Splashworth saw. Afterward he tastes oats. He has learned to blink through them. He has not learned to stop them. He tells no one.

trait.name: Resolute Dampness
trait.description: Maintains optimal felt moisture under pressure. While other moppets wilt or dry out in crisis situations, Fluffington's felt stays immaculately hydrated: a physical manifestation of his refusal to show weakness. Some interpret this as natural composure. Drizzle recognizes it as something else entirely: the body performing calm while the mind won't look at what's underneath.

title.name: The Keeper of Seals
title.authority: Unknown. Title exists in Puddle Navy hierarchy but function and current holder are undocumented.
title.history: Mentioned in naval records but details lost or suppressed.

title.name: Admiral
title.description: The highest rank in the Puddle Navy. Admiral Fluffington holds it now; Admirals Splashworth and Stuffington held it in the war.
title.authority: Highest rank in the Puddle Navy. Commands flagship and fleet operations.

title.name: Chief Engineer
title.description: Head of engineering aboard a Puddle Navy ship. On the USS Fuzzball, Wrinkles.
title.authority: Oversees engineering operations and maintenance on naval vessels.

title.name: Navigator
title.description: Plots a ship's course. On the USS Fuzzball, Pip.
title.authority: Responsible for ship navigation and course plotting.

title.name: Weapons Officer
title.description: Commands a ship's weapons. On the USS Fuzzball, Thud.
title.authority: Commands ship weapons systems and combat operations.

title.name: Communications Officer
title.description: Runs a ship's communications. On the USS Fuzzball, Squeaky, who has a very deep voice.

title.name: Medical Officer
title.description: Looks after the crew's health, and their felt. On the USS Fuzzball, Doc Stitch.
title.authority: Provides medical care and felt repair to crew.

title.name: Helmsman
title.description: Steers the ship. On the USS Fuzzball, Rudder.

title.name: Marine Commander
title.description: Leads a ship's marines and its boarding parties. On the USS Fuzzball, Sergeant Flop.
title.authority: Leads boarding parties and shipboard security forces.

language.name: Standard Moppet
language.description: The common language of moppet space, written and spoken the same in Puddleton and on Feltropolis. The Crumbler's three-word message went out in plain Standard, and The Claw still spent six weeks looking for the encryption.

law.name: The Dry Statute
law.description: A wartime law forbidding moppets to get wet. Every moppet breaks it every day.
law.declaration: No moppet shall enter a puddle, a fountain, a bath or the rain without a permit. Permits are issued by the Administration on Feltropolis Level 5. The office has never issued one.
law.purpose: Passed in Year 14 BT to keep Navy boarding parties dry enough to survive aboard Dry One ships. It was never repealed, because nobody can find the office that repeals things.
law.author: 0695db83-c6e8-7ab6-8000-bf4b7d713f37

law.name: Treaty of Soft Landings
law.description: The foundational peace accord ending The Great Puddle War. Signed Year 0. Celebrated every year at the Year Zero Anniversary.
law.declaration: The foundational legal document of modern moppet civilization, signed at Year 0 to end The Great Puddle War. Celebrated annually as a triumph of diplomacy. Key provisions: Article 1 establishes Feltropolis as neutral territory. Article 3 creates the Treaty Council with jurisdiction over classified wartime matters. Article 5 mandates integration of surviving Dry Ones into Puddle Moppet society. Article 7 bans weaponized crumbs and dissolves the Baking Guilds. Article 9 is classified, sealed by the Treaty Council.
law.purpose: Maintains 200 years of peace. Every institution in moppet space derives authority from it.

event.name: Treaty of Soft Landings
event.description: Peace agreement ending The Great Puddle War, enabling the felt technology revolution.

event.name: Battle of Damp Ridge
event.description: Admiral Splashworth's famous victory during The Great Puddle War. Won against impossible odds. His tactics from this battle are still taught at the Naval Academy in Puddleton.
event.history: Decisive battle that turned the tide of the war. Occurred 27 BT.
event.consequences: Made Splashworth a legend. The Navy built its whole self-image on this one battle. Which makes the truth about his death much worse.

event.name: The Great Puddle War
event.description: The war between the puddle civilization and the Dry Ones over access to the Eternal Drip. It ended with the Treaty of Soft Landings, Year 0 YSL.

event.name: Founding of Feltropolis
event.description: One year after the Treaty of Soft Landings, construction crews from both former belligerents arrived at the neutral asteroid that would become Feltropolis. The first orbital felt-loom was strung in zero-G during the founding ceremony. Two former soldiers, one from each side, threaded the first warp threads together. Their names were not recorded.
event.history: The asteroid had been surveyed during the war as a potential staging post and rejected by both sides as too neutral. After the Treaty it was selected for that exact reason.
event.consequences: Established Feltropolis as the manufacturing center of the post-Treaty era. The seven-level structure was complete by Year 14 YSL.

event.name: First Eternal Drip Pressure Drop Recorded
event.description: Year 198 YSL. Lieutenant Pip, then fourteen and serving as junior navigation cadet on the USS Fuzzball, begins her notebook. The first entry reads: Tuesday, station pressure nine point ninety-eight, expected ten. Re-check tomorrow.
event.history: Pip's first thirty pages are uncorrected. From page thirty-one onward she begins cross-referencing with the Felt Exchange's published Puddle Futures pricing.
event.consequences: Her notebook becomes, by Year 203 YSL, the only continuous five-year pressure record in moppet civilization. Several Guild employees keep notes of the same kind, but they keep them separately, and they do not share.

event.name: The Crumbler's Three-Word Message
event.description: Year 203 YSL, day twelve. Three-word transmission received from the Stale Vengeance over the Cookie Pirates' old trade channel. Plain Standard. The Claw spent six weeks attempting to decrypt the encryption that was not present. Eventually a junior cryptographer pointed out the message had been readable since reception.
event.consequences: Triggered the entire arc of the Year 203 to 210 YSL crisis. The Claw subsequently restructured its decryption protocols to include a plaintext-check pass before encryption-analysis, which would have saved time.

event.name: Siege of the Felt Mills
event.description: Major siege during The Great Puddle War, in Year 15 BT.
event.history: Both sides needed the mills. Neither side wanted to burn them down. That made it a siege instead of a rout.

event.name: Soggy Sock Incident
event.description: Year 203 YSL. Skipper Snoot arrives at The Soggy Sock with half a cookie jammed in his eyepatch socket and a feral moppet on a zero-G felt leash. He has been past the Crumblefields into a previously unknown Bakerfolk ruin called The Rolling Pin, three kilometers long and humming. He brought back a fragment: warm, smells like cinnamon. When Pip held it up, her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds. Eyes don't DO that. Her calculations show the fragment's resonance matches the Eternal Drip's pump cycle. The next morning, The Crumbler sent three words: "We're coming home." Damages: one barstool (feral moppet), two mugs (Snoot's gesturing), and Drizzle's peace of mind (irreplaceable).
event.consequences: Pip's discovery connects The Rolling Pin to the Eternal Drip - confirming Bakerfolk technology underlies moppet civilization. The Crumbler's message signals Cookie Pirates returning from exile. These two facts together will shatter the political order within months.

event.name: The Crumblefield Standoff
event.description: Year 197 YSL. The USS Fuzzball encountered the Stale Vengeance at the edge of the Crumblefields during a routine patrol. Admiral Fluffington ordered battle stations. The Crumbler responded by steering directly into the densest crumb cloud. Fluffington pursued for exactly forty seconds before Chief Engineer Wrinkles pointed out that weapons fire in the Crumblefields would ignite the compressed sugar particles, creating a chain detonation that would destroy both ships and probably reshape the local geography. Both ships withdrew. Fluffington logged it as tactical repositioning. The Crumbler didn't log it at all, because Cookie Pirates don't do paperwork. Sergeant Flop reportedly said, "I could have taken them seventeen times during the retreat." Nobody agreed.
event.consequences: Established an unofficial no-fire zone in the Crumblefields. The Crumbler now uses the area as a buffer, knowing the Navy won't risk engagement there. Fluffington has never returned to the area. The Crumblefields are effectively Cookie Pirate territory by mutual unspoken agreement.

event.name: Eternal Drip Failure
event.description: The machine behind the Eternal Drip is breaking down. Water pressure is dropping 0.3% a year, barely detectable. Pip has been tracking it for five years, 1.5% in all. Nobody else is measuring. If the Drip fails, moppets will starve, since they absorb moisture for nutrition. The Dry Ones' knowledge of surviving without water, suppressed after the Treaty, may be what is needed.
event.consequences: Water shortage and famine. A political crisis when the truth about the Drip comes out. Possibly war over the remaining water.

event.name: The Incident
event.description: Year 120 YSL. The moment everything broke. Skipper Snoot and Admiral Fluffington were fellow officers, friends, maybe more than friends, when Snoot stumbled onto evidence of the Moistened Valley Massacre cover-up. He wanted the truth. Fluffington wanted to protect the Navy (and his father's memory). The confrontation was emotional and political, not physical. Snoot left the Puddle Navy that night with proof hidden somewhere. Fluffington let him go, or couldn't stop him, or both. Neither of them has been the same since. The Incident is what the Navy calls it, because naming it properly would mean admitting something happened.
event.consequences: Snoot became a rogue explorer carrying hidden evidence. The Fluffington-Snoot rivalry began - not petty, but existential. The Claw began monitoring Snoot. The cover-up's first real crack appeared, though it took another 80 years for anyone else to notice.

event.name: Moistened Valley Massacre
event.description: What Skipper Snoot, and a few others, call the final engagement of The Great Puddle War, in the Moistened Valley, two years before the Treaty. The official history says there was no massacre.
event.history: Final major event of The Great Puddle War, two years before the Treaty.
event.challenges: Splashworth's attempt to stop it failed.
event.consequences: The Treaty of Soft Landings was signed two years later, and Feltropolis was founded as neutral territory. Two hundred years of peace followed. The Dry Ones who fled to the Snack Nebula became the Cookie Pirates.

phenomenon.name: Googly Eye Consciousness
phenomenon.description: Googly eyes are functional organs connected to moppet consciousness and soul. The liquid inside contains the floating pupil and is linked to the moppet's sense of self. Pupil movements are involuntary responses - eyes wobble when moppets lie. Googly Eye Technology amplifies what's naturally there. Removing an eye is not just physical damage but soul damage - removing part of consciousness itself. Transplanted eyes carry fragments of previous owner's consciousness (Fluffington has Splashworth's left eye and experiences his memories).
phenomenon.expression: Googly eyes function as both sensory organs and the primary interface for moppet consciousness. Pupil movement reflects emotional and mental state: a still eye is always a bad sign.
phenomenon.effects: Removing an eye takes something out of a moppet that doesn't grow back. Transplanted eyes sometimes carry fragments of the previous owner's consciousness, which is either a gift or a haunting depending on who they were. Eyes can be calibrated and amplified for use in technology. Ancient eyes appear to preserve consciousness across long spans of time, which raises questions nobody in the Navy wants raised.
phenomenon.mythology: Moppet eyes are where the soul actually lives. Not a metaphor. The Bakerfolk seem to have known this. Whether they built the googly eye for that reason, or discovered it by accident, is not recorded.

narrative.name: Stuffington Is Alive
narrative.description: The official history says Admiral Stuffington died in the war. He did not.
narrative.story: Admiral Stuffington did not die in the war. He has been held in The Locked Room on Feltropolis Level 7 since the Treaty was signed. The Treaty Council keeps him there, and keeps the record that calls him a dead war hero. His son does not know.
narrative.consequences: As long as the Council holds him, the official history stands.

narrative.name: What Happened in the Moistened Valley
narrative.description: What the Moistened Valley Account leaves out.
narrative.story: In the Moistened Valley the Dry Ones had surrendered and the Treaty terms were agreed. Admiral Stuffington ordered the attack anyway. Admiral Splashworth tried to stop it, and was killed by his own side on Stuffington's orders. The Treaty of Soft Landings was written over all of it. Drizzle, who tends bar at The Soggy Sock, saw it and will not speak of it. Skipper Snoot found the proof, left the Navy with it, and hid it. Professor Fuzz has spent forty years circling the same facts without knowing what he has. Admiral Fluffington has either always known or has only just found out.
narrative.consequences: The Moistened Valley Account, taught at the Naval Academy, says none of this happened.

narrative.name: The Mother Is Hungry
narrative.description: Why the Eternal Drip exists, and why it is failing.
narrative.story: The Eternal Drip was not built to water anyone. The Bakerfolk built its pumps to feed the Mother, a sourdough starter the size of a lake in the reservoir below, and the moppets have been drinking her runoff ever since. The Drip is failing because she is hungry. Nobody in Moppetopia knows she is there.
narrative.consequences: Whatever the moppets do about the water, they will have to do it about her.

narrative.name: Moppetopia
narrative.story:
Felt sailors, a water world, and a nebula of stale cookies. Two hundred years after the Treaty of Soft Landings ended the Great Puddle War, the Puddle Navy keeps the peace from the USS Fuzzball, the Eternal Drip keeps everyone damp, and Admiral Fluffington and Skipper Snoot are still not speaking.
