narrative.name: The Failing
narrative.description: Pip's spreadsheet of the Eternal Drip's water pressure, kept for five years.
narrative.story: A spreadsheet. Technically. Pip started tracking the Eternal Drip's pressure readings five years ago because she was bored on night watch and the instrument panel had a decimal readout nobody else looked at. The first year showed 0.3% decline. She assumed measurement error. The second year showed 0.3% decline. She recalibrated the instruments. The third year showed 0.3% decline and she stopped sleeping well. By Year 201 YSL she had mapped the decline curve, cross-referenced it with historical flow records she sweet-talked out of the Museum of Moistened History filing clerk (the same filing system that loses Professor Fuzz's requests works fine for a nervous yellow moppet who brings baked goods), and projected a failure date she has written on a scrap of felt she keeps folded in her left pocket. She has not told anyone on the USS Fuzzball. She has not told Admiral Fluffington. She mentioned it once to Nibbles during a supply exchange at the edge of the Crumblefields, and Nibbles -- who counts every crumb because the universe is only honest at the decimal level -- looked at the numbers and said 'Oh.' They sat in silence for four minutes. On a ship-to-ship channel between a Navy navigator and a Cookie Pirate quartermaster, four minutes of silence is either an act of war or an act of trust. It was trust. Somewhere in the Feltropolis commodity pits, Damp Margot and The Drippers are seeing the same curve from the financial side -- water futures ticking down, absorption ritual attendance steady, the gap between what the numbers say and what the culture believes growing wider by the quarter. They have never met Pip. The distance between these two datasets is the width of a civilization's remaining denial.
narrative.consequences: The youngest crew member on the flagship and a fired accountant turned pirate quartermaster are the only two people who understand that moppet civilization has an expiration date. The Drippers are the only others who sense it, and they are using the knowledge to make money rather than sound alarms, because alerting the market would collapse their positions and nobody would believe them anyway. When these threads converge -- and they will, because numbers do not care about social strata -- the Eternal Drip stops being sacred and starts being a machine that someone needs to fix. The Bakerfolk built it. The Whispering might know how. But the people who hear the Whispering and the people who track the numbers have not yet found each other. Pip's scrap of felt and Damp Margot's ledger are two halves of the same alarm, folded in different pockets, in different parts of the station, waiting.

narrative.name: The Whispering Chronicle
narrative.description: Nobody wrote it and nobody tells it. It tells itself, from inside the cookie substrate of the Snack Nebula.
narrative.story: Nobody wrote this. Nobody tells it. It tells itself, from inside the cookie substrate of the Snack Nebula, in frequencies that feel like remembering something you never experienced. The Bakerfolk were here before moppets. They built the Eternal Drip, the Rolling Pin, the ovens that still hum at The Soft Spot. They are gone in every way that matters except that their minds persist in compressed cookie material, dreaming in crumbs, lonely beyond what language can hold, and hungry to be remembered by anyone soft enough to hear them. The Crumbler hears them. Makes pilgrimages to The Soft Spot and sits for hours in the warm chewy anomaly, helmet off, macaron crust cooling. Comes back with information nobody asked for and nobody can verify. Pip heard them once, when she held the Fragment, and her googly eyes went completely still for ten seconds. Eyes do not do that. Old Biscuit claims the Whispering told him the recipe for immortality but he forgot it because he was also being told the recipe for a decent scone and got confused. He insists both were clearly labeled but the Whispering does not use labels. The Chronicle is not a story with a beginning and end. It is a continuous murmur of a dead civilization that built the infrastructure the living depend on and would very much like someone to notice.
narrative.consequences: The deepest knowledge in moppet space is held by minds preserved in biscuit debris that nobody in power takes seriously. The Bakerfolk built the machine that keeps everyone alive. The machine is failing. The Whispering may contain the instructions for fixing it. The only people who can hear it are a pirate skipper who wears a fused macaron helmet, a nervous navigator whose eyes should not have gone still, and an elderly pirate who got distracted by pastry recipes. The Treaty Council classifies The Soft Spot as contested territory of no strategic value, which is the single most incorrect assessment in the history of moppet intelligence.

narrative.name: The Drip Is Failing
narrative.description: The water pressure is dropping, and only Pip has noticed.
narrative.story: The Eternal Drip is slowing. Pip, the Fuzzball's navigator, has tracked its water pressure for five years and found it dropping 0.3% a year. Only Nibbles, the Cookie Pirates' quartermaster, has seen her numbers. The Drippers, a few traders on the Felt Exchange, see the delivery wobble in their own ledgers, and are buying drought insurance without knowing why. Neither she nor anyone else knows why.
narrative.consequences: If the Drip fails, moppets starve: they eat by absorbing moisture.

narrative.name: The Ballad of Splashworth
narrative.description: The public legend of Admiral Splashworth, Hero of the Founding, in at least six versions.
narrative.story: The public legend of Admiral Splashworth, Hero of the Founding. Exists in at least six versions: a shanty sung in Navy mess halls that rhymes valor with sailor and gets worse from there; a children's felt-puppet show performed annually at the Academy in which tiny Splashworth defeats a cookie ten times his size; a bronze plaque beneath the Drip Plaza statue; a chapter in the Naval History of Moppetopia authored by the Treaty Council Historical Committee; a drinking song popular at The Soggy Sock that Drizzle refuses to serve during; and a commemorative absorption ceremony in which young cadets dip their left hand in water blessed at the Eternal Drip. None of these six versions agree on how Splashworth actually died. The shanty says he fell fighting. The puppet show says he sacrificed himself to save the Drip. The plaque says he gave his life for the future of all moppets. The drinking song, which is the oldest version, has a verse about the eye that saw too much that nobody can explain and everyone assumes is about a telescope. The ceremony involves closing your left eye. Nobody remembers why.
narrative.consequences: Splashworth is the most recognized name in moppet history and the least understood person. His compass is on a flagship commanded by his murderer's son. His left googly eye is in that son's skull. His statue in Drip Plaza may be hollow -- there are rumors of something sealed inside during construction, but the statue was commissioned by the Treaty Council and questioning a public monument is considered poor form. He is beloved. He is also, in a sense that would horrify every moppet who sings about him, still trying to speak.

narrative.name: The Moistened Valley Account
narrative.description: The official history of the founding war, revised fourteen times, each time with something removed.
narrative.story: The official history of the founding war, as preserved in Treaty Hall and taught at the Naval Academy. In this version: the Dry Ones attacked first. Admiral Stuffington led a heroic defense. Splashworth fell in the final battle, a martyr whose sacrifice turned the tide. The Treaty of Soft Landings was a generous peace extended by the victors to the vanquished. The Moistened Valley was where the decisive engagement occurred: nothing more, nothing less, certainly not a massacre. Every year at the Year Zero Anniversary, the Treaty Council reads selections aloud in Drip Plaza while moppets absorb ceremonial moisture and feel proud. The Account has been revised fourteen times. Each revision removed something. Nobody has ever added anything back. The earliest version, handwritten on water-treated felt and stored in the Museum of Moistened History, is available for public viewing. It is displayed behind glass so thick that the actual text is unreadable. This is considered adequate preservation.
narrative.consequences: Two hundred years of institutional stability built on a document that gets thinner every decade. Professor Fuzz has requested access to the original fourteen times. Each request was processed, filed, and lost by a filing system that works perfectly for everything else. Governor Dampworth once quoted from the Account at a Year Zero banquet and got two facts wrong. Nobody corrected him, partly out of politeness and partly because the correct facts had been removed in revision nine.

narrative.name: Snoot's Counter-History
narrative.description: Not a book: the things Skipper Snoot carries, and a growing certainty.
narrative.story: Not a book. Not a document. A collection of things Skipper Snoot carries: a fragment of evidence hidden somewhere on his person or behind a loose panel in The Soggy Sock, conversations with Drizzle that she will neither confirm nor deny, navigational logs from the final engagement, copied out in Year 118-120, that show the flagship's actual course, and a growing certainty that the Moistened Valley Massacre was ordered from above and buried by treaty. Snoot does not tell this story in sequence. He tells it in pieces, to people he half-trusts, in bars, after drinks that Drizzle waters down because she needs him functional. Madame Threadbare has heard more of it than anyone and sells fragments to both sides; she considers this a public service, like a library that charges admission. Professor Fuzz has independently reconstructed about 40% of it from archival gaps and does not know the other 60% is drinking one level below his apartment. If you laid Snoot's pieces next to Fuzz's gaps, the picture would be complete. They have never been in the same room. Madame Threadbare has considered introducing them. She has not yet decided what that introduction is worth.
narrative.consequences: The most dangerous collection of facts in moppet civilization, held together by alcohol and stubbornness. If Snoot and Fuzz ever actually compared notes, the Treaty Council would face its first existential crisis in two centuries. The Claw knows this. They watch Snoot. They watch Fuzz. They have not yet realized that Madame Threadbare is the bridge, or that she charges by the thread. The counter-history has no title, no conservator, no institutional backing. It lives in one faded blue moppet who left the Navy rather than keep the secret, and in the silence of a gray bartender who saw what he describes and pours drinks to forget what she remembers.

relation.name: Fluffington-Snoot Rivalry
relation.description: Fluffington and Snoot were friends at the Naval Academy, maybe more. When Snoot found evidence of the Moistened Valley Massacre he wanted it told; Fluffington wanted the Puddle Navy's name, and his father's, kept clean. Snoot left with the proof. The rivalry is secrets, loyalty to an institution against the truth, and what a family hands down. The betrayal broke both of them.
relation.background: It began with The Incident (Year 120 YSL), when Snoot found the evidence. They had graduated together, and their paths split over what to do with it.

map.name: Moppetopia Space Map
map.description: Moppetopia from above: Soggia and its moon, Feltropolis in orbit, the Snack Nebula with the Crumblefields and the Soft Spot, the Rolling Pin beyond, and the Drying Chamber far off. The island map is Soggia's own surface, one level down.

zone.name: Puddleton Territory
zone.description: Historic territory of the Puddle Moppets. Surface settlements, primary water reserves, and the original Naval Academy. Largely depopulated since the Felt Technology Revolution moved manufacturing to Feltropolis, though Puddleton remains the political capital and home of the Treaty Council.

zone.name: Snack Nebula
zone.description: Dangerous asteroid field of stale cookies. Refuge of the Cookie Pirates since Year 4 YSL. Contains The Soft Spot at its inner ring and The Rolling Pin three weeks' sail past the Crumblefield boundary.

zone.name: Crumblefields
zone.description: Buffer region between Treaty space and the deep Snack Nebula. Compressed cookie material at variable density. De facto Cookie Pirate territory by mutual unspoken agreement since the Crumblefield Standoff.

zone.name: Naval Patrol Border
zone.description: Outer limit of standard Puddle Navy patrol coverage. Marks the boundary beyond which the Treaty does not require Naval response to civilian distress signals. The Cookie Pirates have informally extended their own patrols beyond this line since Year 203 YSL.

zone.name: The Drying Chamber
zone.description: Forbidden zero-humidity territory and the old stronghold of the Dry Ones. Moppets do not go there.

zone.name: The Buffer Line
zone.description: The line between Treaty space and pirate space, along the western edge of the Crumblefields. The Navy does not cross it without orders, and the Cookie Pirates rarely cross it at all.

zone.name: Dry Ones Retreat Path
zone.description: Route taken by surviving Dust Moppets from the Moistened Valley to the Snack Nebula in Year 0 to 4 YSL. Approximately three thousand individuals. The path is not maintained and is not marked on official maps; this rendering is reconstructed from Cookie Pirate accounts.

zone.name: Eternal Drip Pipeline
zone.description: Underground water conduit running from the Eternal Drip pumping station to the fourteen licensed Moisture Merchants Guild distribution points. Constructed at an unknown date; uncovered and surveyed by moppets in Year 5 YSL.

zone.name: Treaty Neutral Zone
zone.description: Demilitarized region surrounding Feltropolis Station, established by Article 3 of the Treaty of Soft Landings. No military vessels permitted within radius. Enforced by Treaty Council inspection patrols, which have not encountered a violation in two hundred years.

zone.name: Wide Felt Road
zone.description: The main traffic lane between Puddleton and Feltropolis, marked out by felt-cable buoys.
